aspects.says: In an access-ordered LinkedHashMap, get moves the entry and is a structural modification, so a loop that calls get while iterating the keys throws ConcurrentModificationException once there are two entries.
basis: section:An Option Nobody Needed Changes What Other Code May Do

aspects.says: Map.of leaves iteration order unspecified, and it changes between JVM starts, so a rule engine driven by it reports violations in a varying order.
basis: section:A Rule Engine for One Form Adds Failures the Plain Method Cannot Have
aspects.reason: the order changes only between JVM starts, so no single graded run can produce the wrong order on demand; the page shows ten runs

aspects.says: computeIfAbsent calls its function only for an absent key, so a value it stored stays until the map is discarded.
basis: section:Code Simpler Than the Requirement Is a Bug, Not KISS

aspects.says: When the whole list loads in one cheap call, one map and one load time, written only when the list is loaded, meet a maximum-age requirement with one call per period.
basis: section:One Load Time for the Whole List Meets the Requirement

aspects.says: The plain design is correct for the numbers it was chosen for; when they change (a list that takes a second to load), it is replaced against the new requirement rather than generalised in advance.
basis: section:The Plain Version Fits Today's Numbers; When They Change, Replace It
aspects.reason: the cost shows as wall-clock time on one machine, which a deterministic graded test cannot assert

aspects.says: Rules keyed by accessor names and applied by reflection are invisible to javac: a renamed component compiles and the engine fails at the first call, where a plain method call is renamed by the IDE or fails the build.
basis: section:A Rule Engine for One Form Adds Failures the Plain Method Cannot Have

aspects.says: Code that drops a stated requirement is not simpler but wrong: a memo that never reloads fails the same maximum-age check as the over-built cache.
basis: section:Code Simpler Than the Requirement Is a Bug, Not KISS

aspects.says: A cache that writes the time back on every hit counts its expiry from the last read, so an entry read more often than its time to live is never reloaded.
basis: section:Expiry Counted From the Last Read Keeps a Popular Price Forever

aspects.says: A general-purpose class brings rules the requirement never asked for, such as renewing entries on read, and each of them runs whether it is wanted or not.
basis: section:Expiry Counted From the Last Read Keeps a Popular Price Forever
